items.title: Ain Dubai: Facts About the World's Tallest Observation Wheel
items.content_text: Ain Dubai, on Bluewaters Island, was recognized by Guinness World Records as the tallest and largest observation wheel in the world at its 2021 opening.

items.title: Cairo Metro Guide: Lines, Tickets, and Tips
items.content_text: The Cairo Metro was the first metro system in Africa and the Middle East. Here is how its lines, tickets, and women-only cars work.

items.title: Dubai Mall: World's Most-Visited Retail Destination
items.content_text: Dubai Mall isn't just a shopping center — it's home to an aquarium, an ice rink, and a waterfall, and draws more annual visitors than most theme parks.

items.title: Dubai Marina: A Complete Guide to the Waterfront District
items.content_text: Dubai Marina is a man-made waterfront district built around an artificial canal, known for its skyscraper skyline, waterfront promenade, and dense residential population.

items.title: Dubai Opera: Inside the Emirate's Performing Arts Venue
items.content_text: Dubai Opera is a multi-format performing arts venue in Downtown Dubai, designed to resemble a traditional dhow boat and hosting opera, concerts, and theater.

items.title: Opening a Bank Account in Egypt: Guide
items.content_text: How foreign residents can open a bank account in Egypt: required documents, choosing a bank, account types, and practical tips for expats and long-term visitors.

items.title: Egypt Customs and Import Rules: A Practical Guide
items.content_text: Bringing goods into Egypt, whether personal items or commercial shipments, involves Egyptian Customs Authority rules on duty-free allowances, declarations, and duties.

items.title: Egypt Driving Guide: Rentals & Road Rules
items.content_text: Should you rent a car in Egypt? Car rental requirements, an International Driving Permit, road conditions, and why most visitors use drivers instead in 2026.

items.title: Home Internet in Egypt: A Practical Broadband Guide
items.content_text: Fixed home internet in Egypt is offered by several providers using fiber, DSL, or 4G/5G fixed wireless, with plans and pricing varying widely by area and technology.

items.title: Mobile Wallets in Egypt: How They Work
items.content_text: Mobile wallets like Vodafone Cash and InstaPay have grown fast in Egypt as digital alternatives to cash for everyday payments.

items.title: Egypt's National ID Card: What It Is and Why It Matters
items.content_text: Egypt's national ID card is a mandatory identity document for citizens and residents, required for banking, healthcare, and most official transactions.

items.title: Can Foreigners Own Property in Egypt? A Practical Guide
items.content_text: Foreigners can legally own property in Egypt under specific conditions, including restrictions on location, size, and resale timing that vary by property type.

items.title: Egypt's Universal Health Insurance System: What to Know
items.content_text: Egypt has been rolling out a Universal Health Insurance system since 2019, gradually replacing the older health insurance scheme governorate by governorate.

items.title: How Foreigners Get a Work Permit in Egypt
items.content_text: Foreigners working in Egypt generally need both a work permit from the Ministry of Manpower and a residence permit, usually sponsored by an Egyptian employer.

items.title: Global Village Dubai: A Complete Guide
items.content_text: Global Village is a seasonal cultural and entertainment park in Dubai where dozens of countries run themed pavilions of shopping, food, and shows.

items.title: The History of Emoji
items.content_text: Emoji originated in late-1990s Japan and are now standardized worldwide by the Unicode Consortium so they display consistently across devices.

items.title: The History of Stop-Motion and Claymation Animation
items.content_text: Stop-motion animation predates cartoon animation and relies on photographing tiny physical movements frame by frame. Here's how the technique evolved.

items.title: The History of the Adhan, Islam's Call to Prayer
items.content_text: The adhan, Islam's call to prayer, traces to the earliest years of the Muslim community in Medina and is traditionally linked to a companion of the Prophet Muhammad.

items.title: The History of the Crossword Puzzle
items.content_text: The modern crossword puzzle traces to a 1913 word-cross puzzle published in a New York newspaper, and it became a global pastime within about a decade.

items.title: The History of the Drive-In Movie Theater
items.content_text: The drive-in movie theater was patented in 1933 as a way for families to watch films without leaving their cars. Here's how it rose and later declined.
